books.section: Unit 5: Toward the Civil War and Reconstruction (1844–1877)

stimulus.text: A color lithograph published in 1870, titled “The Fifteenth Amendment. Celebrated May 19th, 1870.” At the center, a parade fills a city street with marching soldiers, a band, and a carriage. Around the border are small scenes: a classroom full of Black children with their teacher, a wedding, a Black man casting a ballot, and Black men in formal dress. Portraits in oval frames around the border include President Ulysses S. Grant, Vice President Schuyler Colfax, and Abraham Lincoln.
stimulus.source_note: Thomas Kelly, publisher, “The Fifteenth Amendment. Celebrated May 19th, 1870,” lithograph after a design by James C. Beard, 1870 (Library of Congress, LCCN2003690776). Public domain. Image viewed before writing; scenes and portraits described from the image itself.

source: original; stimulus as noted in stimulus.source_note
stem: One limit of the celebration in this print is that the Fifteenth Amendment

options.text: freed enslaved people in the border states.

options.text: applied only to the Northern states.

gave the vote to former Confederates.

rationales.A: Background: the Thirteenth Amendment, not the Fifteenth, ended slavery in the border states.
rationales.B: Background: the amendment bound the whole country, North and South alike.
rationales.C: The amendment bars denying the vote on account of race, color, or previous servitude, and says nothing about sex. Black women and white women alike still could not vote, which split the women’s movement over whether to support it.
rationales.D: Background: former Confederates were not given the vote by this amendment; many had never lost it.
rationales.general:
1. Read what the amendment actually bars: denial of the vote on account of race, color, or previous servitude.
2. Sex is not on that list.
3. Background: women would wait until the Nineteenth Amendment in 1920.
4. So the print’s celebration is real, but it leaves half the population outside the frame.
Remember: a right granted “on account of” one thing may still be denied on account of another.
